Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates asymmetry in pulmonary vascularity with a smaller, oligemic right lung and prominent left pulmonary vasculature, which are classic signs of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or hypoplasia associated with Takayasu arteritis. This is corroborated by the CT image (Figure 2b) showing calcification and narrowing of the right pulmonary artery, indicating a longstanding process rather than an acute embolic event.
